section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the two verses that allude to Lag BaOmer, describing the "gal" (heap) as a partition between upper and lower realms, and how Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai clarified this partition to allow revelation even in the lower worlds.
section.t: And this is the connection of the two verses in which the concept of Lag BaOmer is hinted,
"Unveil my eyes and I will behold wonders from Your Torah" and "this heap is witness,"
for the heap between Lavan and Yaakov is analogous to the decree and partition between the upper and lower realms that existed before the giving of the Torah.
And it is explained in the Siddur, Shaar HaLag BaOmer,
that regarding the heap between Lavan and Yaakov,
there are two matters.
The heap between the upper Lavan
(who is above Yaakov)
and Yaakov,
and it is the partition between the worlds of Ein Sof that are above Atzilus and Atzilus.
And the heap between Yaakov and the lower Lavan,
the partition between Atzilus and BiYA.
And the hint of Lag BaOmer in this verse is,
that through Rashbi the heap and partition were clarified,
the partition between the upper Lavan and Yaakov and also the partition between Yaakov and the lower Lavan.
That is,
that even in BiYA and even in the world of Asiyah there will be a revelation of Atzilus and also a revelation of the Ein Sof that is above Atzilus.
And this concept is also the content of the second verse that hints at Lag BaOmer,
"Unveil my eyes and I will behold wonders from Your Torah,"
that even in the matters of the revealed part of Torah
(BiYA),
and also in the "garment of Torah,"
in the narratives of Torah
(Asiyah),
there will be a revelation of the wonders of Torah,
the aspect of the soul of Torah
(Atzilus)
and also the aspect of the soul of the soul
(above Atzilus).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the partition was made as a "gal" (heap) rather than a wall to indicate that the ultimate purpose of the partition is for subsequent connection, and that the hint of Lag BaOmer in "this heap is witness" reveals the inner intent of the tzimtzum itself.
section.t: And to add,
based on the known principle that all matters in the Torah are with utmost precision,
it must be said,
that this that the verse "this heap is witness"
[which speaks about the matter of the heap and partition between Lavan and Yaakov]
hints at Lag BaOmer, whose concept is the clarification of the heap and partition,
is,
because the sign and testimony regarding "I will not pass over to you... you will not pass over to me"
was that they made a heap,
and not that they made a wall,
is to hint that the making of the partition from the outset is in a manner that there is room for "I will pass over to you and you will pass over to me."
That is,
that the intention in making the partition between the upper and lower realms from the outset is so that afterward there will be the connection of the upper and lower realms.
And this that initially there had to be a partition between the upper and lower realms,
is,
because the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is that the dwelling place will be in a lower realm beneath which there is no lower,
and therefore the lower realms came into being through a partition,

not only that in actuality the revelation of the upper realms does not shine in them, but that there is a partition between them which is a sign and testimony that it will be "I will not pass over to you and you will not pass over to me,"
so that through the service of Yisrael there will be the connection even of these lower realms
[regarding which there is a decree
that they should not connect with the upper realms]
with the upper realms.
And this is that the hint of Lag BaOmer is in the verse "this heap is witness,"
for this that Rashbi clarified the heap and partition is that through him the inner aspect of the tzimtzum itself was revealed,
that the intention in the tzimtzum
[which is its inner aspect]
is for the sake of revelation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the two verses, explaining that the revelation of wonders through "unveil my eyes" is enabled by the Lag BaOmer concept of the inner purpose of tzimtzum being for revelation.
section.t: And this is that the hint of Lag BaOmer in the verse "Unveil my eyes and I will behold wonders from Your Torah" is learned from the hint of Lag BaOmer in the verse "this heap is witness,"
for the main innovation and elevation of "Unveil my eyes and I will behold wonders from Your Torah" is that the seeing of the wonders of Torah will be
(not only because the wonders will be revealed,
but rather)
through "unveil my eyes,"
that the Holy One, blessed be He, will open the eyes of the person and the person will see the wonders of Torah from the perspective of the person's own being
(as above, section 4),
and in order that the lower person will be able to see the wonders of Torah from his own perspective,
it is through the concept of Lag BaOmer hinted in "this heap is witness" – the revelation of the inner aspect of the tzimtzum,
that the tzimtzum is for the sake of revelation.
